question: In February 2021, In which of the following cases did the Court observe that Consent of a family is not needed once two adults decide to marry?
option_1: Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana
option_2: Rahul Sharma v. National Insurance Company Ltd.
option_3: Devilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh
option_4: Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka
solution_text:
The correct answer is Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In February 2021, the Supreme Court of India (Bench of Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul), in Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka, held that once two adult individuals consent to marry each other, the consent of the family, community or clan is not necessary. (लक्ष्मीबाई चंदारागी मामला — वयस्क विवाह में परिवार की सहमति आवश्यक नहीं)

 

• The case involved a couple who married against the wishes of the woman's family and sought police protection after facing threats and pressure to annul the marriage.

 

• The Court reaffirmed that the right to marry a person of one's choice is integral to Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) of the Constitution.

 

• It directed police authorities across states to ensure protection to adult couples who marry out of their own free will, irrespective of caste or community objections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This ruling is in line with earlier landmark judgments such as Shafin Jahan v. Asokan K.M. (2018) (the 'Hadiya case') and Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018), both of which upheld an adult's right to choose a life partner and directed action against honour-based violence, including by khap panchayats.

 

NOTE

 

• Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana (Option 1): This 2021 Supreme Court case dealt with the interpretation of Sections 304B and 498A IPC relating to dowry death and cruelty, not with consent for adult marriage.

 

• Rahul Sharma v. National Insurance Company Ltd. (Option 2): This is an insurance-claim related matter and is unconnected to the issue of consent in marriage.

 

• Devilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): This case does not pertain to the question of family consent for the marriage of two adults.

question: Which of the following organic compounds is synonymous with olefiant gas which is used to make anaesthetics, refrigerants and other chemicals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethylene.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethylene (C₂H₄) is historically known as olefiant gas (meaning 'oil-forming gas' in French/Dutch), a name given because it forms an oily liquid, Dutch liquid (1,2-dichloroethane), when combined with chlorine. (एथिलीन — ओलिफिएंट गैस)

 

• It is a colourless, flammable hydrocarbon (alkene) with a double bond between two carbon atoms.

 

• Ethylene is a key industrial feedstock, used to manufacture anaesthetics, refrigerants, antifreeze, and plastics such as polyethylene.

 

• It is also a naturally occurring plant hormone that regulates fruit ripening, flowering, and senescence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ethylene was one of the first gases used as a general anaesthetic in surgery before being largely replaced by safer agents.

 

• Polymerisation of ethylene under high pressure/catalysis produces polyethylene (polythene), the most widely used plastic in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• 1-Pentene (Option 2): A five-carbon alkene, used mainly as a co-monomer in polymer manufacturing; it is not called olefiant gas.

 

• Methane (Option 3): The simplest alkane (CH₄), the main component of natural gas; it has no carbon-carbon double bond and is unrelated to the term olefiant gas.

 

• Butane (Option 4): A four-carbon alkane used as a fuel (e.g., in LPG and lighters); it is also not termed olefiant gas.

question: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Godavari river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mahi river is NOT a tributary of the Godavari. It is an independent, west-flowing river that originates in the Vindhya Range in Madhya Pradesh and flows through Rajasthan and Gujarat before draining into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). (माही नदी — गोदावरी की सहायक नदी नहीं)

 

• The Godavari, the largest peninsular river of India, rises at Trimbakeshwar, Nashik (Maharashtra) and flows into the Bay of Bengal, and is fed by several major tributaries.

 

• Pranhita is the largest tributary of the Godavari by volume, formed by the confluence of the Penganga, Wardha and Wainganga rivers.

 

• Manjra and Purna are also genuine right-bank tributaries of the Godavari, flowing through Maharashtra, Telangana and Karnataka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important tributaries of the Godavari include the Indravati, Sabari, Pranhita (left-bank) and Manjra, Purna (right-bank).

 

• The Godavari basin is the second-largest river basin in India after the Ganga, and the river is often called 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganges of the South).

 

NOTE

 

• Pranhita (Option 2): A genuine, in fact the largest, tributary of the Godavari, so it is not the correct answer to this 'NOT a tributary' question.

 

• Manjra (Option 3): A genuine right-bank tributary of the Godavari, so it is not the correct answer.

 

• Purna (Option 4): A genuine right-bank tributary of the Godavari in Maharashtra, so it is not the correct answer.

question: What is the significance of 26 January being chosen as a day to celebrate the Republic Day, aside from the adoption of the constitution?
option_2: Foundation day of the Indian National Congress
solution_text:
The correct answer is Declaration of Purna Swaraj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress (December 1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Congress adopted the resolution demanding 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence). (पूर्ण स्वराज घोषणा — 26 जनवरी 1930)

 

• 26 January 1930 was subsequently observed across the country as 'Purna Swaraj Diwas' (Independence Day), with the tricolour hoisted and the pledge for complete independence taken.

 

• When India's Constitution was ready, 26 January 1950 was deliberately chosen as the date to bring it into force, to honour this earlier 1930 declaration.

 

• This is why Republic Day (26 January) is distinct from Independence Day (15 August), which instead marks the actual date of freedom from British rule in 1947.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day/Samvidhan Diwas), but it came into effect on 26 January 1950.

 

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Revolution of 1857 (Option 1): The First War of Indian Independence began on 10 May 1857 at Meerut, unrelated to 26 January.

 

• Foundation day of the Indian National Congress (Option 2): The INC was founded on 28 December 1885 in Bombay, not on 26 January.

 

• Day of the Champaran Satyagraha (Option 4): Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha began in 1917 and has no link to 26 January.

question: During the reign of Akbar, ________ was the land that has lain fallow for three or four years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chachar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Akbar's land revenue system, described in the Ain-i-Akbari by Abul Fazl, agricultural land was classified into four categories based on cultivation status. Chachar referred to land that had lain fallow for three or four years. (चाचर भूमि — तीन-चार वर्ष परती)

 

• Polaj was land that was cultivated every year, continuously, without being left fallow.

 

• Parauti was land left fallow for a short period (about one year) to allow it to regain fertility, before being cultivated again.

 

• Banjar was land left uncultivated for five years or more (barren/wasteland).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The land revenue (Kharaj) was assessed through Akbar's finance minister Raja Todar Mal's Zabt/Dahsala system, which fixed rates based on average produce and prices of the preceding ten years.

 

• Different rates of assessment applied depending on which of these four categories a plot of land fell into, reflecting its productivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Parauti (Option 1): This refers to land fallow for about a year to recover fertility, not the three-to-four-year fallow period described in the question.

 

• Polaj (Option 2): This is annually and continuously cultivated land, the opposite of fallow land.

 

• Banjar (Option 4): This refers to land uncultivated for five years or more, a longer period than the three-to-four years described.

question: What is the age criteria for the subscribers of Atal Pension Yojana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18-40 Years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is a government-backed pension scheme, launched on 9 May 2015, open to Indian citizens aged between 18 and 40 years. (अटल पेंशन योजना — 18-40 वर्ष आयु सीमा)

 

• It is administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) and primarily targets workers in the unorganised sector.

 

• Subscribers contribute periodically until the age of 60, after which they receive a guaranteed minimum monthly pension ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000, depending on the contribution slab chosen.

 

• A bank account and Aadhaar/mobile number linkage are required to enrol in the scheme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• On the death of the subscriber, the spouse is entitled to the same pension amount, and thereafter the accumulated corpus is paid to the nominee.

 

• APY replaced the earlier Swavalamban Yojana as the government's flagship pension scheme for the unorganised sector.

 

NOTE

 

• 20-30 Years (Option 1): This range is narrower than and does not match the scheme's actual eligibility window.

 

• 25-35 Years (Option 2): This range also does not correspond to the scheme's official eligibility criteria.

 

• 40-60 Years (Option 4): Subscribers must join before turning 40 (up to age 40 at entry) and continue contributing until 60; this range does not describe the entry eligibility.

question: Dr DS Athwal was known as the 'Father of ______ Revolution in India'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wheat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Dilbagh Singh Athwal, an agricultural scientist at Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana, is known as the 'Father of Wheat Revolution in India'. (गेहूं क्रांति के जनक — डॉ. दिलबाग सिंह अठवाल)

 

• He played a pioneering role in developing and popularising high-yielding, semi-dwarf wheat varieties in India during the 1960s, using material derived from Norman Borlaug's Mexican wheat strains.

 

• His work substantially boosted wheat productivity in Punjab and neighbouring states, forming a key part of India's Green Revolution.

 

• Dr. Athwal later moved to the United States and continued his contributions to agricultural science before passing away there.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. M. S. Swaminathan is widely regarded as the overall 'Father of the Green Revolution in India', having led the broader institutional and policy effort alongside scientists like Dr. Athwal.

 

• Norman Borlaug, the American agronomist, is known globally as the 'Father of the Green Revolution' for developing high-yield disease-resistant wheat varieties.

 

NOTE

 

• Oilseed (Option 1): This is not the field associated with Dr. Athwal; he is specifically linked to wheat.

 

• Rice (Option 2): Rice revolution contributors are typically associated with other scientists (e.g., work at IRRI/ICAR on rice varieties), not Dr. Athwal.

 

• Millet (Option 3): Millets are not the crop associated with Dr. Athwal's pioneering work.

question:
Which of the following can be considered as an example of flow variable?

(i) Production of rice

(ii) Import of cloth

(iii) Change in capital
solution_text:
The correct answer is All of (i), (ii) and (iii).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A flow variable is an economic quantity that is measured per unit of time (over a period), unlike a stock variable, which is measured at a specific point in time. (प्रवाह चर — समयावधि में मापा गया)

 

• Production of rice (i) is a flow variable, as it is measured over a given period, e.g., per year or per season.

 

• Import of cloth (ii) is also a flow variable, since imports are recorded over a specific duration, such as a month or a year.

 

• Change in capital (iii) is a flow variable — it represents investment, i.e., the addition to the capital stock over a period of time, even though capital itself (the stock) is measured at a point in time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common examples of stock variables include wealth, capital, money supply, and population — all measured at a particular moment.

 

• Common examples of flow variables include income, expenditure, savings, production, and investment — all measured over a duration.

 

NOTE

 

• None of (i), (ii) and (iii) (Option 1): Incorrect, since all three examples given are in fact flow variables.

 

• Only (iii) (Option 2): Incorrect, because production of rice and import of cloth are also flow variables, not just change in capital.

 

• Only (i) and (ii) (Option 4): Incorrect, because change in capital (investment) is also a flow variable, so it should be included as well.

question: How many main styles of Chhau folk dance exist?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian martial-dance form found in eastern India, and it exists in three main styles, each named after its region of origin. (छऊ नृत्य — तीन प्रमुख शैलियाँ)

 

• Seraikella Chhau (from Seraikella, Jharkhand) uses masks and is known for its fluid, graceful movements.

 

• Purulia Chhau (from Purulia, West Bengal) also uses elaborate masks and is more vigorous/martial in style.

 

• Mayurbhanj Chhau (from Mayurbhanj, Odisha) is distinctive in that it is performed without masks, relying entirely on facial expressions and body movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhau dance was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

• The dance form combines martial arts, athletics, and folk and tribal dance traditions, and is traditionally performed during regional festivals such as the Chaitra Parva.

 

NOTE

 

• 7, 9, and 5 (Options 1, 3 and 4): None of these numbers corresponds to the recognised classification of Chhau dance, which comprises exactly three main styles — Seraikella, Purulia and Mayurbhanj.

question: Which of the following countries will host the para badminton championship in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thailand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2023 BWF Para Badminton World Championships were hosted by Thailand, held in the city of Pattaya in February 2023. (पैरा बैडमिंटन विश्व चैंपियनशिप 2023 — थाईलैंड)

 

• The event is organised by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) and features para-badminton categories across different disability classifications.

 

• India has produced notable para-badminton champions, such as Pramod Bhagat, Manasi Joshi, and Krishna Nagar, who have won medals at various editions of this championship.

 

• Para badminton made its Paralympic debut at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Badminton World Federation (BWF) is headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

 

• The 2024 BWF Para-Badminton World Championships were held in Pattaya, Thailand as well, before the Paris 2024 Paralympics.

 

NOTE

 

• China (Option 1): China did not host the 2023 edition of the Para Badminton World Championships.

 

• India (Option 2): India has not hosted the Para Badminton World Championships, though it hosts other badminton tournaments.

 

• Indonesia (Option 4): Indonesia did not host the 2023 Para Badminton World Championships.

question: Who among the following freedom fighters lost his life during the protest against Simon Commission where black flags were waved at the Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lala Lajpat Rai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Simon Commission, an all-British commission with no Indian members, arrived in India in 1928, prompting nationwide protests under the slogan 'Simon Go Back' and demonstrations with black flags. (लाला लाजपत राय — साइमन कमीशन विरोध)

 

• At Lahore on 30 October 1928, Lala Lajpat Rai led a peaceful protest march against the Commission, during which he was severely beaten in a lathi-charge ordered by police officer James A. Scott.

 

• He succumbed to his injuries on 17 November 1928, and his death is widely believed to have fuelled revolutionary anger, later leading to the assassination of J. P. Saunders by Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev in revenge.

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai was popularly known as 'Punjab Kesari' (Lion of Punjab) and was a prominent member of the extremist trio 'Lal-Bal-Pal' (with Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Simon Commission's recommendations eventually fed into the Government of India Act, 1935.

 

• The Indian National Congress's response to the all-white Simon Commission also spurred the formation of the Nehru Report (1928), India's own constitutional blueprint.

 

NOTE

 

• Chittaranjan Das (Option 2): A prominent nationalist leader and founder of the Swaraj Party, he died in 1925, before the Simon Commission's arrival in 1928.

 

• Sachindra Nath Sanyal (Option 3): A revolutionary associated with the Hindustan Republican Association; he was not the person fatally injured in the Simon Commission protest.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee (Option 4): A moderate Congress leader and founder of the Indian National Association; he was not involved in or a casualty of the Simon Commission protests.

question:
Select the correct option about Kwashiorkor.

Statement A: It is a form of malnutrition caused by a lack of fat in the diet.

Statement B: Children who develop Kwashiorkor may not grow or develop properly and may remain stunted for the rest of their lives.
option_2: Both statements A and B are correct
option_3: Both statements A and B are incorrect
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only statement B is correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kwashiorkor is a severe form of malnutrition caused by an inadequate intake of protein in the diet, despite roughly adequate calorie/energy intake — not a lack of fat. (क्वाशिओरकोर — प्रोटीन की कमी से कुपोषण)

 

• Statement A is incorrect: It wrongly attributes Kwashiorkor to a lack of fat, whereas the actual cause is a deficiency of protein.

 

• Statement B is correct: Children affected by Kwashiorkor, especially during critical growth years, can suffer impaired growth and development, and may remain permanently stunted.

 

• Key symptoms of Kwashiorkor include edema (swelling, especially of the belly and legs), fatty liver, skin and hair changes, and a distended abdomen.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Marasmus, another form of protein-energy malnutrition, is caused by a deficiency of both calories and protein, leading to severe wasting rather than the edema seen in Kwashiorkor.

 

• The word 'Kwashiorkor' originates from the Ga language of Ghana, roughly meaning 'the sickness the baby gets when the new baby comes', referring to displacement from breastfeeding.

 

NOTE

 

• Both statements A and B are correct (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement A misidentifies the cause as fat deficiency rather than protein deficiency.

 

• Both statements A and B are incorrect (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement B is factually accurate regarding stunted growth in affected children.

 

• Only statement A is correct (Option 4): Incorrect, since Statement A wrongly attributes the disease to fat deficiency instead of protein deficiency.

question: In Which year did John Newlands propound the 'Law of Octaves' an innovative concept proposing the periodicity of chemical elements arranged in the order of atomic weight?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1865.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• English chemist John Alexander Reina Newlands proposed the 'Law of Octaves' in 1865. (न्यूलैंड्स का अष्टक नियम — 1865)

 

• According to this law, when elements are arranged in increasing order of atomic weight, every eighth element exhibits properties similar to the first, analogous to the eighth note in a musical octave.

 

• This was one of the earliest attempts at classifying elements based on a periodic pattern, and it worked reasonably well only for the lighter elements known at the time.

 

• The law broke down for heavier elements and was largely criticised and dismissed by contemporaries, though it is now recognised as a precursor to Mendeleev's Periodic Law (1869).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dmitri Mendeleev formulated the modern Periodic Table in 1869, arranging elements by atomic weight and leaving gaps for undiscovered elements.

 

• The modern periodic law, based on atomic number rather than atomic weight, was proposed by Henry Moseley in 1913.

 

NOTE

 

• 1861, 1863, and 1867 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these years corresponds to Newlands' proposal of the Law of Octaves, which he presented to the Chemical Society in 1865.

question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with fundamental rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35) deals with Fundamental Rights, often called the 'Magna Carta of India'. (भाग III — मौलिक अधिकार)

 

• It originally guaranteed seven fundamental rights; the Right to Property was removed from this list by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 and made a legal right under Article 300-A.

 

• The rights currently guaranteed include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

• Article 32, which empowers citizens to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of these rights, was described by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Rights are enforceable in a court of law, unlike the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV), which are non-justiciable.

 

• The concept of Fundamental Rights was borrowed from the Constitution of the United States.

 

NOTE

 

• Part IX (Option 1): Deals with the Panchayats (local self-government in rural areas).

 

• Part VI (Option 2): Deals with the State Government (Governor, State Executive, State Legislature and High Courts).

 

• Part XI (Option 3): Deals with relations between the Union and the States, covering legislative and administrative relations.

question: FTX Crypto Cup is associated with which of the following sports events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chess.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FTX Crypto Cup was a chess tournament, part of the Champions Chess Tour / Magnus Carlsen Chess Tour, sponsored by the cryptocurrency exchange FTX. (एफटीएक्स क्रिप्टो कप — शतरंज टूर्नामेंट)

 

• It featured leading grandmasters, including world champion Magnus Carlsen, competing in an online rapid chess format.

 

• The tournament was part of a broader series of online chess events that gained popularity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

• It reflected the growing trend of cryptocurrency and fintech companies sponsoring major sporting and mind-sport events in the early 2020s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Champions Chess Tour is an elite online rapid chess circuit organised by Play Magnus Group/Chess.com, featuring top-ranked grandmasters worldwide.

 

• FTX, the cryptocurrency exchange that sponsored this event, collapsed in November 2022 amid a major financial scandal.

 

NOTE

 

• Snooker (Option 1): The FTX Crypto Cup was not a snooker event; it was a chess tournament.

 

• Billiards (Option 3): Billiards is a separate cue sport and is unrelated to the FTX Crypto Cup.

 

• Golf (Option 4): The FTX Crypto Cup had no association with golf.

question: Who among the following won the Padma award for the year 2023 for his efforts of reviving the traditional art of making Etikoppaka toys by adoption of eco-friendly technologies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CV Raju.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C. V. Raju, a grassroots innovator from Etikoppaka, Andhra Pradesh, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 for reviving the traditional craft of Etikoppaka wooden toys using eco-friendly, non-toxic, vegetable-dye-based lacquer techniques. (सीवी राजू — एटिकोप्पका खिलौने, पद्म श्री 2023)

 

• Etikoppaka toys are traditional lacquered wooden toys from Andhra Pradesh, made using softwood (Ankudu wood) and natural, child-safe dyes.

 

• His innovations aimed at making the toy-making process safer and more sustainable, moving away from harmful chemical dyes traditionally used.

 

• He was recognised alongside other grassroots innovators honoured for science-and-technology-based approaches to reviving traditional Indian crafts and art forms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, conferred for distinguished contribution in various fields including art, social work, and science.

 

• Etikoppaka is a village in the Anakapalli district of Andhra Pradesh, famed for this centuries-old craft, sometimes called 'Etikoppaka Bommalu'.

 

NOTE

 

• Victor Banerjee (Option 1): A well-known Indian actor, unconnected to Etikoppaka toy-making.

 

• Devendra Jhajharia (Option 2): A celebrated Indian Paralympic javelin thrower and Padma Bhushan awardee, unrelated to this craft.

 

• Radheyshyam Khemka (Option 3): Not associated with the revival of Etikoppaka toys.

question: The finance commission of India is required to make recommendations to the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is President of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India every five years (or earlier if needed). (वित्त आयोग — राष्ट्रपति को सिफारिशें)

 

• The Commission is required to make recommendations to the President regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States, and the principles governing grants-in-aid to States.

 

• The President then causes these recommendations, along with an explanatory memorandum, to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

 

• The Finance Commission also recommends measures needed to augment a State's Consolidated Fund to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 16th Finance Commission, chaired by Arvind Panagariya, was constituted to give recommendations for the period 2026-31.

 

• The recommendations of the Finance Commission are generally advisory in nature, not binding on the government, though they are usually accepted.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 2): The Finance Commission's recommendations are constitutionally addressed to the President, not directly to the Ministry of Finance.

 

• Parliament (Option 3): While the recommendations are eventually laid before Parliament by the President, the Commission's constitutional mandate is to report to the President.

 

• Central Cabinet (Option 4): The Commission does not submit its recommendations to the Cabinet; its constitutional addressee is the President.

question: What do you call the glycocalyx when it is like a loose sheath in the cell envelope of bacteria?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Slime layer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The glycocalyx is the outermost, viscous coating surrounding the cell wall of many bacteria, composed mainly of polysaccharides. When it is loose, unorganised, and diffuse (not firmly attached), it is called the slime layer. (श्लेष्मा परत/स्लाइम लेयर — ढीला ग्लाइकोकैलिक्स)

 

• When the glycocalyx is instead thick, well-organised, and firmly attached to the cell wall, it is termed a capsule.

 

• The slime layer helps bacteria in attachment to surfaces, protection against desiccation, and evasion of the host immune system, though less effectively than a true capsule.

 

• It also plays a role in biofilm formation, allowing bacterial cells to adhere to each other and to surfaces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A prominent example of a capsule-forming bacterium is Streptococcus pneumoniae, whose capsule is a major virulence factor.

 

• The glycocalyx (capsule/slime layer) is distinct from the cell wall and plasma membrane, lying external to both.

 

NOTE

 

• Mesoderm (Option 1): This is a germ layer found in animal embryonic development, entirely unrelated to bacterial cell structure.

 

• Capsule (Option 2): This term applies when the glycocalyx is thick and firmly organised, not when it is loose, which is the scenario described.

 

• Organelle (Option 4): Bacteria (prokaryotes) generally lack membrane-bound organelles; the glycocalyx is an extracellular structure, not an organelle.

question: Aditi Mangal Das was conferred the Mahari Award for dance in 2022 for which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aditi Mangaldas, a veteran and internationally acclaimed Kathak dancer, was conferred the Mahari Award for 2022. (आदिति मंगलदास — कथक नृत्यांगना, महारी पुरस्कार 2022)

 

• The Mahari Award is presented by dance institutions in Odisha in memory of the traditional Mahari dancers (temple dancers), who historically performed in Odisha's temples and are considered precursors to the Odissi dance form.

 

• The award recognises outstanding contributions to Indian classical dance broadly, and is not restricted only to Odissi exponents.

 

• Aditi Mangaldas trained under Kumudini Lakhia and is known for blending traditional Kathak with contemporary choreography.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term 'Mahari' refers to women temple dancers dedicated to deities in Odisha's temples (notably the Jagannath Temple, Puri), whose art is seen as the root of classical Odissi dance.

 

• Aditi Mangaldas runs the 'Drishtikon Dance Foundation' in New Delhi, promoting Kathak and contemporary dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 2): Although the Mahari Award has strong historical roots in the Odissi tradition, Aditi Mangaldas herself is recognised as a Kathak exponent, not an Odissi dancer.

 

• Manipuri (Option 3): Aditi Mangaldas is not associated with the Manipuri dance form.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 4): Aditi Mangaldas is not a Bharatanatyam dancer; her primary classical form is Kathak.

question: The North–South corridor links which of the two major cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Srinagar and Kanyakumari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The North-South Corridor, developed under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP), connects Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) in the north with Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu) in the south. (उत्तर-दक्षिण गलियारा — श्रीनगर से कन्याकुमारी)

 

• It has a total length of about 4,076 km, including a spur connecting Kochi (Kerala) to Salem (Tamil Nadu).

 

• It is implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and is one of the largest highway projects in the country.

 

• The corridor is complemented by the East-West Corridor, which connects Silchar (Assam) to Porbandar (Gujarat).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The North-South and East-West Corridors together with the Golden Quadrilateral (connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata) form the core of the NHDP's initial phases.

 

• The Golden Quadrilateral was the first mega-highway project undertaken under NHDP, launched in 1999.

 

NOTE

 

• Leh and Vishakhapatnam (Option 1): This pairing does not correspond to the officially defined North-South Corridor endpoints.

 

• Leh and Kanyakumari (Option 2): The corridor's northern terminus is Srinagar, not Leh.

 

• Srinagar and Vishakhapatnam (Option 3): The corridor's southern terminus is Kanyakumari, not Vishakhapatnam.

question: Who among the following gave the famous 'Do or Die' slogan during Quit India Movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahatma Gandhi gave the famous 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) call while launching the Quit India Movement on 8 August 1942, at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay (now August Kranti Maidan). (करो या मरो — महात्मा गांधी, भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन)

 

• This speech urged Indians to either secure freedom from British rule or die trying, marking a decisive escalation in the freedom struggle.

 

• The Quit India Movement (Bharat Chhodo Andolan) was launched following the failure of the Cripps Mission to satisfy Indian demands for self-governance.

 

• Gandhi and other top Congress leaders were arrested the very next day (9 August 1942), leading to widespread spontaneous protests across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Quit India Resolution was passed by the All India Congress Committee (AICC) session in Bombay on 8 August 1942.

 

• Following the arrest of top leadership, younger leaders like Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia and Aruna Asaf Ali led the movement underground.

 

NOTE

 

• Abul Kalam Azad (Option 1): He was the Congress President during the Quit India Movement but is not credited with the 'Do or Die' slogan.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 2): A key Congress leader arrested alongside Gandhi in 1942, but the slogan is attributed to Gandhi, not him.

 

• Subhash Chandra Bose (Option 3): He was outside India at the time (leading the INA/Azad Hind Fauj) and gave the separate slogan 'Delhi Chalo' and 'Jai Hind', not 'Do or Die'.

question: Why do most parts of India receive rainfall from June to September?
option_2: Due to extremely cold nights in these regions
option_3: Due to high pressure in these months
solution_text:
The correct answer is Due to the South-West monsoon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Most parts of India receive rainfall between June and September due to the South-West Monsoon, which brings moisture-laden winds from the Indian Ocean. (दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून — जून-सितंबर वर्षा)

 

• This monsoon accounts for about 75-80% of India's total annual rainfall and is critical to Indian agriculture.

 

• It splits into two branches over the Indian landmass: the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch, which together cover most of the subcontinent.

 

• The monsoon results from differential heating of land and sea, creating a low-pressure area over the Indian landmass in summer, which draws in moist oceanic winds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The retreating/North-East Monsoon (October-December) brings rainfall mainly to Tamil Nadu and parts of the southeastern coast, as winds pick up moisture crossing the Bay of Bengal.

 

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) typically declares the onset of the South-West Monsoon over Kerala around 1 June each year.

 

NOTE

 

• Due to extremely cold nights (Option 2): This is not a scientifically valid reason for the June-September rainfall pattern.

 

• Due to high pressure in these months (Option 3): In fact, a low-pressure system over the Indian subcontinent (not high pressure) drives the South-West Monsoon.

 

• Due to the North-east monsoon (Option 4): The North-East Monsoon occurs later in the year (October-December) and affects mainly the southeastern coast, not most of India during June-September.

question: Shivaputra Siddharamayya Komkalimath is the original name of which of the following Indian classical singers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Kumar Gandharva.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Kumar Gandharva, one of the most influential Hindustani classical vocalists of the 20th century, was born as Shivaputra Siddharamayya Komkalimath in 1924 in Karnataka. (पंडित कुमार गंधर्व — मूल नाम शिवपुत्र सिद्धारमैया कोमकलिमठ)

 

• He earned the title 'Kumar Gandharva' (meaning 'celestial musician') as a child prodigy for his extraordinary singing talent.

 

• He is renowned for developing his own distinctive, unconventional gayaki (singing style) after recovering from tuberculosis, diverging from strict traditional gharana norms.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contributions to Hindustani classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kumar Gandharva is also known for his compositions based on the poetry of saints like Kabir (e.g., 'Nirbhay Nirgun') and folk traditions of Malwa.

 

• He settled in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh, where he spent much of his creative life.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Omkarnath Thakur (Option 1): A noted vocalist of the Gwalior gharana, but this was not his birth name.

 

• Pandit Jasraj (Option 3): A renowned classical vocalist of the Mewati gharana, whose birth name was Jasraj, not Komkalimath.

 

• Pandit Dinkar Kaikini (Option 4): A respected vocalist and musicologist, but this is not his original name either.

question: The national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at ________ per capita per month for urban areas of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹1,000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Tendulkar Committee methodology, India's national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at ₹1,000 per capita per month for urban areas. (गरीबी रेखा 2011-12 — शहरी ₹1,000 प्रति व्यक्ति प्रति माह)

 

• The corresponding rural poverty line for the same year was estimated at ₹816 per capita per month.

 

• The Tendulkar Committee, headed by economist Suresh Tendulkar, revised the earlier calorie-based methodology to a broader consumption-expenditure basket including food, education, health and other essential items.

 

• Based on this line, national poverty estimates for 2011-12 placed roughly 21.9% of India's population below the poverty line.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rangarajan Committee (2014), set up subsequently, proposed a revised (higher) poverty line of about ₹1,407 per month in urban areas and ₹972 in rural areas, though its recommendations were not officially adopted for poverty estimation.

 

• Poverty estimation in India has historically evolved through several expert groups, including the Lakdawala Committee and later the Tendulkar and Rangarajan Committees.

 

NOTE

 

• ₹3,000, ₹2,000, and ₹1,500 (Options 1, 3 and 4): None of these figures matches the Tendulkar Committee's officially estimated urban poverty line of ₹1,000 per capita per month for 2011-12.

question: Kosala Mahajanapada (6th century BCE) is a part of modern day:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kosala was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas (great kingdoms) of ancient India in the 6th century BCE, and it corresponds broadly to the Awadh region of present-day eastern Uttar Pradesh. (कोशल महाजनपद — वर्तमान उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• Its territory lay along the Sarayu River, bounded by the Gomti and other regions, and its capital was Shravasti (with Ayodhya as another major city).

 

• Kosala holds great religious and epic significance — Ayodhya is celebrated as the birthplace of Lord Rama in the Ramayana, while Shravasti was an important centre associated with Gautama Buddha's teachings.

 

• Kosala eventually rose to prominence under rulers like Prasenajit, and was later absorbed into the Magadha Empire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The sixteen Mahajanapadas are described in early Buddhist and Jain texts such as the Anguttara Nikaya.

 

• Other major Mahajanapadas included Magadha (Bihar), Avanti (Malwa region, Madhya Pradesh), and Vatsa (near Kaushambi, Uttar Pradesh).

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Ancient Mahajanapadas located in this region are not associated with Kosala; the Deccan region had different political entities.

 

• Haryana (Option 2): Kosala is not located in the Haryana region; kingdoms like Kuru were associated with that area.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): The Mahajanapada located here was Avanti (capital Ujjain), not Kosala.
